messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple 5xx spikes observed across our us-west-2 ELB frontends. Auto-detection threshold breached (latency > 1.2s, 5xx rate > 3%). Investigate. Thread opened at 2026-03-15T09:20:34Z
leah-oncall: grabbing. seeing ELB target group health flipping to UNHEALTHY in us-west-2b and increased ENI detach errors in cloud logs.
matt-sre: grabbing logs now. any customer reports?
tiffany-support: several customers reporting elevated latencies and some errors, mostly chat/generate endpoints. tickets routed from support hub.
leah-oncall: quick check: Route53 health checks for edge proxies in us-west-2 are reporting mixed results. Some DNS resolvers returning stale IPs for edge-azb hosts. suspect control-plane or ENI network partitioning in azb.
anya-platform: I see EC2 control-plane error spikes from aws: 'AttachNetworkInterface: timeout' in metrics for us-west-2b. NAT GW metrics also show burst of connection resets.
ryan-eng: is this correlated with autoscaling/redeploys? any recent changes?
sophia-pm: no releases in last hour. metrics show start at 09:18Z.
leah-oncall: mitigation plan: 1) pause new deploys in wsz2 2) shift traffic away from us-west-2b AZ to other AZs and region if needed 3) lower Route53 weight for affected edge endpoints 4) open status page note after triage.
matt-sre: I'll start a traffic shift. calling the runbook: PagerDuty runbook -> https://pagerduty.example/runbooks/azb-network-failures
leah-oncall: matt, runbook step: change Route53 weighted records to move 80% traffic off the affected edge pool. I'll lift healthcheck sensitivity.
matt-sre: running change using cli: 
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345EXAMPLE --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"edge.redwood.example.com.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"usw2a-edge","Weight":80,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.15.22.11"}]}}]}'
```

matt-sre: cli returned ChangeInfo Id: /change/C0ABCDEFG12345 - propagation started. TTL low (30s) to speed transition.
leah-oncall: also increasing ELB healthy threshold to avoid flapping: 
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:...:targetgroup/tg-123 --attributes Key=healthy_threshold_count,Value=5
```

tiffany-support: letting impacted customers know we're investigating. drafting status: "Experiencing elevated errors in us-west-2; traffic being shifted. No data loss, degraded latency for some customers."
sophia-pm: please include ETA of next update in 15m and mention mitigations.
leah-oncall: matt, any progress on ENI issue?
matt-sre: ENI detach errors persist in us-west-2b and host-level logs show repeated DHCP lease failures on a subset of hosts. I'm isolating failing instances and draining them from ELB.
ryan-eng: for our serving runtime, we have KV cache pinned in those hosts. Draining will cause cold KV misses — expect short latency spikes. We can temporarily relax SLOs and add additional warm containers in unaffected AZs.
leah-oncall: good note. anya, can we spin up additional capacity in us-east-1 to absorb cross-region traffic if Route53 weights don't stabilize?
anya-platform: yes we have warm reserved capacity. Initiating cross-region scale to add 30% headroom in us-east-1. Command queued.

pagerduty-bot: Incident assigned to matt-sre and leah-oncall (PD-INC: 987654). Priority P1. Handoff scheduled if >30m.

leah-oncall: matt, after you finish the primary shift, let's do a formal handoff to night oncall. I want a short doc in thread about current hypothesis, mitigation, and follow-ups.
matt-sre: copying key points: hypothesis = AZ-level ENI control-plane degradation causing ELB targets to be removed + partial DNS cache staleness. Mitigation = Route53 weight change (80% -> other AZ), ELB target drain + increase healthy threshold, spawn extra capacity in us-east-1, notify customers.
tiffany-support: posting status update v1 to status.redwood.com: "Partial networking degradation in us-west-2 affecting some regions. Traffic shifted; mitigation in progress. No data loss. Engineers investigating."
sophia-pm: include note that dedicated customers on Reserved capacity in us-west-2 may see failover to dedicated pools in other regions; ops will coordinate billing impacts later.
leah-oncall: we're seeing Route53 change propagate; 5xx rate down from 4.1% -> 1.2% in last 3 mins. RTT still elevated (900ms -> 650ms). Good.
matt-sre: drain completed on 6 instances, new healthy targets in other AZs showing steady becomes healthy after retries.
anya-platform: us-east-1 scale completed. Extra sinks are up. KV cache rebuild in progress.
leah-oncall: handing off to night oncall (ryan-eng) at 09:40Z. Ryan, please take alerts and continue monitoring DNS propagation and ENI errors. I'll stay muted but available if needed.
ryan-eng: I have it. key things to watch: ENI detach error rate, Route53 change status, ELB target health, and customer tickets for edge failures. If 5xx rises >2% re-open with PD.
matt-sre: follow-ups for postmortem: collect ENI attach/detach logs, AWS support case reference, and timeline of Route53 weights.
tiffany-support: customers updated v2: "Mitigation in progress; traffic shifted away from affected AZs. Degraded latency may persist as caches rebuild. Next update in 30 minutes."
leah-oncall: closing loop for now — major impact mitigated, routing stability improving. tagging incident for postmortem. pagerduty-bot: Incident status updated -> mitigated.
ryan-eng: I'll monitor through the handoff window and will escalate if regression. leaving notes here for next shift: TTL lowered to 30s during mitigation; remember to restore normal TTL to 300s after 24h.
leah-oncall: thanks team. postmortem owners: matt-sre (tech), tiffany-support (customer comms), anya-platform (root cause & AWS liaison).
incident-bot: Thread closed at 2026-03-15T09:36:42Z (2139001402).
